[url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/548430/Deep_Rock_Galactic/]Deep Rock Galactic (DRG)[/url] for elves (streamers). Quite literally the same systems from DRG, if not the same code at a superficial level. Instead of a rock solid foundation of picking a kit and shooting bugs however, the gameplay loop is 100% dedicated - in its full, integral entirety - to the most boring part of DRG; slipping downwards in the dark towards an objective while evading the fall damage. The "added spice" is your kit being entirely randomly generated, procure-on-site, low durability versions of the DRG tools (engineer's platform launcher but with 1 charge, the scout's flare gun but with 2 shots, gunner's zipline but with only 1 shot, etc). Also randomly generated Improvised Explosive Devices inside the tiles, that motion trigger when you dig nearby. If your thoughts even slightly entertain the idea of playing this game, [i]immediately[/i] boot up DRG instead. It's the original version; a unique, insanely well optimized game. It elegantly features varied gameplay loops of different objectives, consistent kits of tools to play with, and most importantly: there's a ton of beer to choose from that you can have to irritate mission control with. https://store.steampowered.com/app/548430/Deep_Rock_Galactic/

O jogo se resume a uma premissa simples: seu cachorro caiu num buraco bizarro e você precisa descer as profundezas da terra para resgatá-lo. A mecânica básica envolve cavar, usar explosivos e lidar com a pior força da física: a gravidade. Na teoria, é uma missão de resgate emocionante; na prática, é um simulador de acidentes e traição entre amigos. Pontos positivos: Física duvidosa: Você passa mais tempo caindo de penhascos do que cavando. Comunicação de proximidade: Aproxime o microfone para ouvir os gritos desesperados dos seus amigos enquanto caem na lava. Amizade à prova de bombas: Nada une mais um grupo do que reviver um companheiro para, logo em seguida, jogar uma bomba sem querer (ou de propósito) na cara dele. Se você e seus amigos curtem jogos cooperativos focados em rir dos próprios erros e da incompetência alheia, esse jogo vale cada centavo. O resgate do cachorro vira o menor dos seus problemas perto das risadas e do pânico generalizado.

I picked this up looking for a fun co-op game to play with my family, and it absolutely delivered. The premise is simple: rescue your dog by descending deeper and deeper into a cave system. In practice, it quickly turns into hilarious chaos. Between the physics, gravity, giant worms, bombs, drills, strange items, and accidentally sabotaging each other, every expedition becomes its own story. What I enjoyed most is that the game naturally creates memorable moments instead of forcing them. We weren't trying to be funny—the game simply kept putting us into ridiculous situations. One minute you're carefully making a path for your teammates, the next someone accidentally launches themselves into a pit, summons a giant worm, or drops a bomb at exactly the wrong time. One thing I really appreciated is that the game encourages teamwork without punishing you for having fun. You'll be catching friends before they fall, digging paths for each other, sharing supplies, and then five minutes later accidentally blowing someone up with a bomb or sending them flying with a bad throw. Those unexpected moments are where the game really shines. The art style is charming, the controls are easy to learn, and the physics create just enough unpredictability to keep every expedition feeling fresh. If you're looking for a co-op game that creates hilarious stories with friends and family instead of relying on scripted moments, Pratfall is an easy recommendation. Every expedition feels different because the fun comes from the situations you create together. My only recommendation would be to bring friends or family. While it can be played solo, this is one of those games that's at its best when everyone is laughing together over the latest disaster. Definitely recommended.

A lot of reviews aptly sum this game up as Deep Rock Galactic with the progression style of Peak. I would disagree that it’s an exact mash-up of these two things. Pratfall seems much more centric to the idea of ragebaiting your friends by setting off items or throwing things at your friends muppet style heads. Hearing the substantial thunk, and then seeing them ragdoll through the air is hilarious. We tend to spend the first half hour of our sessions just goofing off above ground doing this. However, outside of the novelties of pickaxing your way down, this game offers a bit too many hazards that take a lot of the agency out of your run. In Peak, if I were to fail it’s usually because I mismanaged my resources or failed to account for the well telegraphed hazards. In Pratfall, my carefully planned-out traversal has often been ended outside of my control due to multiple drill mines completely removing the floor from beneath me. This is especially frustrating during the ice level since it’s much longer than the other levels. In a level that already has enough new hazards to make it interesting, it feels less like gaining a mastery over your skills to progress, and more like gambling on the right paths to take. I would consider playing more frequently if the devs adjust these things, along with replacing the absurd frequency of bats on the hot rock level with something that fits thematically and adds a comparable level of difficulty instead. If these are addressed in future patches along with new content/features to the game, I see the game being a staple for me and my friends
